key_concepts.summary: Orthodox vs southpaw creates an open-stance matchup where rear hands and lead feet become central tactical variables.
Outside lead-foot position can open lines, but it should be taught as positioning and angle, not careless stepping.
Open-stance matchups often create clearer rear-hand lanes and different defensive responsibilities.
The lead-hand battle and lead shoulder position change jab path, parry, and entry decisions.
Beginners need stance recognition, safety, and simple outside-step awareness before complex traps.
Foot clashes and balance errors rise when fatigue reduces stance discipline.

tactical_rules.rule: First teach the user to identify orthodox, southpaw, closed stance, and open stance.
Teach outside lead-foot position as a simple angle concept before building traps.
In open stance, rear-hand defense and rear-hand attack both become higher priority.
Do not let users chase outside foot by crossing feet or reaching.
Open stance can make jab lanes different; use jab to chest/body or hand-fight when head jab is blocked.
Open-stance rear-hand attacks should include an exit or angle because return fire is available.
Beginners should not receive complex southpaw trap sequences until basic footwork is stable.
When tired, simplify to stance recognition, jab, guard, and exit rather than elaborate angle chains.

physical_demands.quality: Hip and trunk control to step outside without losing punch mechanics.
Short reactive steps and pivots to win or recover foot position.
Recognize stance, lead-foot relation, and rear-hand threat quickly.
Guard endurance against rear-hand lane threats.
Lateral hip and groin capacity for angle changes.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Open-stance lead-foot battles can create foot clashes, stumbles, or ankle irritation.
Reaching for outside foot without hip turn can stress the knee.
Unprepared users can be hit by rear hands from unfamiliar angles.
Beginners may freeze if given too many stance-matchup rules.
Fatigue increases crossing feet and stance loss.

training_implications.summary: Beginner: identify stance, maintain base, avoid crossing feet, jab and exit.
Intermediate: outside foot, rear-hand lane, lead-hand battle, pivot exit, simple counters.
Advanced: opponent-specific stance traps, feints, counters, and score-state adjustments.
Store stance_matchup, lead_foot_relation, rear_hand_lane, and foot_clash_risk as retrieval tags.
Assess stance recognition, foot discipline, rear-hand defense, and exit quality.
